name: Site visit report
what: What a tour of the property found that the documents did not show.

fields.label: Attendees
fields.definition: Who toured and who showed the property, by role, such as the sponsor, the listing broker, the property manager or a tenant contact.

fields.label: Areas seen
fields.definition: The buildings, suites, roofs, yards and mechanical areas actually entered or viewed.

fields.label: Areas not seen
fields.definition: Spaces that were locked, occupied or skipped, and why; a later visit or the condition consultant covers them.

fields.label: Occupancy observed
fields.definition: Which spaces looked in use and which looked empty or dark, compared suite by suite with the rent roll.

fields.label: Use observed
fields.definition: What each tenant appeared to be doing in the space, including outdoor storage, chemicals, drums, tanks or processes that differ from the permitted use in the lease.

fields.label: Condition observed
fields.definition: Visible condition of the roof, walls, slab, paving, doors, docks and building systems, such as stains, cracks, ponding or patched areas, each with its location.

fields.label: Building features observed
fields.definition: Features read on site rather than from the offering, such as clear height, number and type of dock and grade doors, power service, sprinklers and parking.

fields.label: Access and surroundings
fields.definition: Truck access, curb cuts, drainage, neighboring uses and anything on adjoining land that could affect the property.

fields.label: Differences from the documents
fields.definition: Each thing seen that the offering, rent roll, leases or reports did not show or showed differently, with the document it contradicts.

fields.label: Photos
fields.definition: Where the tour photos are stored, with a note of what each set shows.

fields.label: Follow-up questions
fields.definition: Questions for the broker, seller, tenants or consultants that the tour raised, and who is to answer each.
